parsed.summary: The file formalizes Theorem 1.1. It asserts a nonempty finite family F of connected, bipartite, non-acyclic graphs such that each member F has ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} eventually (with c uniform over F), while ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}). It also asserts that F is not compact and that the corrected Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture fails. The definitions (F-freeness via Mathlib `Free`, `familyExtremal` as a finite sup, `IsCompactFamily` matching (1)) faithfully encode the paper's notions. There is no substantive caveat; the statements are at least as strong as the paper's.

glossary.plain: A finite simple graph on vertex set {0,…,order−1}.
Host G on n vertices contains no member of 𝓕 as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph.
glossary.note: Mathlib `A.Free B` means ¬(A ⊑ B), i.e. B has no copy of A; the direction is correct.

glossary.plain: ex(n,𝓕): maximum number of edges of an 𝓕-free graph on n vertices.
glossary.note: The sup over a finite set is fine. The empty graph is always 𝓕-free for families of cyclic graphs, so the sup is never over an empty set.

glossary.plain: There exist F∈𝓕 and C>0 with ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n,𝓕) for all sufficiently large n.
Every finite nonempty family of graphs each containing a cycle is compact.
For every F∈𝓕, eventually c·n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F).
glossary.note: The constant c is uniform over the family, which is harmless for a finite family.

lean_claims.plain: The corrected compactness conjecture is false: some finite nonempty family of graphs each containing a cycle is not compact.

There exist a nonempty finite family 𝓕 of connected bipartite graphs each containing a cycle, and c, C > 0, such that: (i) for every F∈𝓕, eventually c·n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F); (ii) for all n, every 𝓕-free graph on n vertices has e^16 ≤ C·n^21; (iii) ex(n,𝓕)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; (iv) the trivial identities 1/48 > 0 and 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48 hold; (v) 𝓕 is not compact; and (vi) the compactness conjecture fails.

There exist a nonempty finite family 𝓕 of connected bipartite graphs each containing a cycle, and c>0, such that every member has ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} eventually, ex(n,𝓕) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) as n→∞, 𝓕 is not compact, and the compactness conjecture fails.

paper_claims.plain: There exists a finite nonempty family 𝓕 of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,𝓕)=O(n^{4/3−1/48}) and ex(n,F)=Ω(n^{4/3}) for every F∈𝓕; in particular no member satisfies (1).
There exist a connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for large n.

coverage.why: The big-O upper bound, eventual per-member lower bound, member properties and non-compactness all match.
The upper bound holds for all n with an explicit constant (exponent 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48), not just asymptotically.

flags.explanation: The upper bound e^16 ≤ C n^21 is stated for all n rather than eventually. This is stronger than the paper's O(·) and fine, since finitely many small n can be absorbed into C. Lines 66–67 are trivial arithmetic padding, and line 65 is redundant given line 63.

lint_verdicts.why: edgeFinset of a graph on Fin n is a genuine finite set, so its card is the true edge count.
(4:ℝ)/3 is real division with a nonzero denominator.
Finite edge set; the card is the true edge count.
Real division by 48 ≠ 0; trivially true padding conjunct.
Real literals with nonzero denominators; the identity 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48 is genuinely true.
The exponent is the real number 4/3 − 1/48 = 21/16; 0^positive = 0 at n = 0 is irrelevant under atTop.
